notes: Reached via Chrome connector, no issues (robots.txt: standard disallows only, no Claude-specific block). Site is a Next.js app; every browse/category page embeds a search-result JSON in #__NEXT_DATA__ (props.pageProps.initialData.searchResult) with itemStacks[0].meta.totalItemCount and a breadCrumb array giving the true parent chain -- this was the primary qty AND tree-verification source, since the rendered header text is capped at 'N+' (e.g. 'Sofas & Couches (70+)') and is not exact on its own. For every leaf, totalItemCount was cross-checked against the rendered '(N+)' header (matched every time) and, for the largest node (Sofas & Couches, 70), against a raw two-page item enumeration (46 unique ids page1 + 25 unique ids page2 = 71 raw vs 70 reported, the 1-item gap being a duplicate ad-slot tile) -- confirms totalItemCount is the reliable count on this platform, consistent with the prior Home-Decor pass's finding for this same site. Tree discovery: walked the mega-menu Departments>Home>Furniture 'Shop by Room' hub (Living Room, Bedroom, Kitchen & Dining, Office, Game Room, Kids), then MANDATORILY cross-checked via sitemap_categories.xml (268 furniture-keyword URLs) per brief Trap #1 -- this surfaced two entire branches invisible from the room-tile hub: 'Folding & Stackable Furniture' (a top-level Furniture-department child, 5 real leaves) and 'Small Space Furniture' (a cross-merchandising bucket; excluded itself but its one clean non-duplicate child 'Entryway Furniture & Accent Storage Cabinets' kept). Also found 'Bookcases & Shelves' (6) which breadcrumbs under Office Furniture -- NOT added as a separate row since it is a subset already inside the Office Furniture total of 67 (adding both would double-count). Excluded as marketing/cross-merchandise rollups (not real single-purpose categories, each overlaps already-counted true categories and/or mixes non-furniture): 'Home Entertainment' (25+, mixes sofas/TV stands already counted plus non-furniture digital calendars), 'Small Space Furniture' (45+, mixes beds/dining sets/rugs already counted elsewhere), 'Labor Day Outdoor Savings' aka /browse/outdoor-furniture/10250142 (a Savings/Clearance bucket mixing furniture with grills and cold-plunge tubs), "Member's Mark Patio Chairs & Outdoor Decor" (a brand-merchandising bucket, not a real 'Patio Chairs & Benches' category despite the misleading slug). Excluded as non-furniture: Mattresses, Rugs (textile), Outdoor Shades & Structures/Decor & Accents/Lawn & Garden/Sheds & Outdoor Storage/Outdoor Play/Spas Saunas & Cold Plunges/Fire Pits & Outdoor Heaters (none are furniture by the brief's rules). 'Kids Furniture' (28) and 'Gaming Furniture and Desks' (30) are genuine single site nodes but each mixes a minority of non-furniture items (play gym/storage organizers/foam flooring in Kids; none major in Gaming) or duplicates another counted node (Gaming Furniture and Desks includes 2 gaming chairs also counted in the separate 'Gaming Chairs' leaf) -- both flagged rather than silently adjusted, per Rule 1's null/flag guidance and the brief's SKU-overlap precedent (documented, not deduped, since exact ID diffing across nodes was not performed). 'Vanities & Bathroom Furniture' (30) is the site's dedicated bathroom-furniture category (breadcrumb Home>Bath, so labelled category="Bathroom Furniture"); of its 30 items ~27 are genuine freestanding vanity cabinets (brief explicitly includes vanity units/cabinets) and ~3 are non-furniture (a shower base, an over-toilet shelf rack, a door-handle hardware pack) -- flagged. Outdoor furniture lives under a separate 'Outdoor & Patio' department, not 'Furniture': 'Outdoor Seating' (110+ header) is itself a parent with 4 real distinct child URLs (confirmed via breadcrumb parent id 4550105 on each), so it is emitted as a grouping row, not a leaf; 'Outdoor Dining Sets' (41) is a sibling leaf with no further split (only in-page seating-capacity/shape filters, not real subcategories -- confirmed no URL change on interaction). Sanity checks per Rule 4 applied throughout: numbers changed per category (rejecting any constant/site-wide value), no suspiciously round numbers, h1/breadcrumb matched the requested node on every page, sponsored tiles visible in grids were not counted (totalItemCount is a JSON field independent of ad injection).
